observations: body L1-L8: Nallino restores p. 78, L29-L32, where the italic words of p. 78 («eo utere ut supra iis 5ᵖ ¼; invenies hypotenusam Lunae aequatam ad declivitatem epicycli») are what the codex and Plato keep of the passage; the words he supplies stand in brackets and in italics. Dividing 5ᵖ 15′ by the sine of the apparent semidiameter of the epicycle and multiplying by 60ᵖ gives NE = NK : sin NEK, the distance of the centre of the epicycle (p. 254, L22-L24).

body L9-L27: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the two epicycles about A and about N (radius 30.9 and 31.0 pt) on the line from the Earth E to H′ (A and N 0.3 and 0.1 pt off it), the lines EG′, EG and G′G, the perpendiculars M′G′ and MG (89.8° and 89.7° to the line) and the radii AG′ and NG; the bold italic letters stand where they are printed. The anomaly is drawn the same in both epicycles (H′AG′ 66.5°, HNG 66.6°), so that G′G is parallel and equal to AN (0.3° off); hence the angle EG′G equals H′EG′, an equation of the epicycle, at most 5° 1′ (L21-L22).

body L12-L13, L23: «adn. d» is note d) of p. 253; «AG′ = 5ᵖ ¼» is the radius of the epicycle, 5ᵖ 15′; «adn. g» is the next note, on p. 79, L7. In L23 the g is followed by a comma, and the dash before «Cum» measures 9.8 pt.
body L15-L16: a speck after the full stop of «EG.» is not transcribed; the comma after «qua re» prints high.

body L17-L20: the bars after «AE» (L17, 10.3 pt, at the end of the line), after «60ᵖ» (L18), after «EG′» (L19) and between the brackets (L20) are minus signs. «portio duplae excentricitatis» is al-Battānī's name, p. 79, L6: 60ᵖ less the distance NE.
body L28-L31: a heavy bracket closes Schiaparelli's addition, after a dash of 10.2 pt; «al–Battānī», «78–79» and «334–36» have long dashes (5.4, 5.8 and 5.5 pt).

body L32-L40: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the circle about the Earth E (radius 77.4 pt) and the eccentric about F (radius 61.0 pt), touching at A (0.7 pt apart), the line from A through F and E, the epicycle about N (radius 23.4 pt), whose centre lies on the eccentric, the line from H through N and E to L, the perpendicular FL (88.9° to NL), and the lines NF, GE and GN, with the bold italic letters where they are printed. A dot to the right of A is not drawn. As drawn, FE : FA is 14.6 : 61.4 = 0.24 (Ptolemy's lunar model, 10ᵖ 19′ : 49ᵖ 41′ = 0.21) and the angle AEN is 135.5°.

body L33-L40: the angle FEL is the supplement of AEN, the double elongation, so that sin FEL = sin 2 (☾ − ⊙); in the right triangle FEL, FL and EL are ε sin and ε cos 2 (☾ − ⊙) on the radius R. On p. 79, L1-L4 al-Battānī takes the square of FL from 2468ᵖ 26′, the square of 49ᵖ 41′, and adds or subtracts EL: NE = NL ∓ EL. The bars between ☾ and ⊙ and after «180°» are minus signs; «ε» is printed upright.
notes L1: «p. 78, l. 24» is «Radix alterutro modo reperta est hypotenusa Lunae, scilicet distantia Lunae a centro Terrae».
